mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a first-generation EA111 1.4 TSI (CAV/CTH), expect £2,500-£4,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £500-£1,200 for a used engine. For second-generation EA211 1.5 TSI (DADA/DPC), rebuilt units typically range £3,000-£5,000, with used options from £600-£1,400. Fitting adds approximately £520-£650 labour at UK specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign on EA111 1.4 TSI engines is a rattling noise on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds. This is the tensioner losing hydraulic pressure. Other symptoms include P0011 fault code (camshaft/crankshaft correlation), engine management light illumination, and eventually misfiring or non-start if the chain jumps.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your Tiguan's value. First-generation examples (2007-2016) worth under £5,000: a used engine at £500-£1,200 plus fitting often makes more sense than a rebuilt unit. On second-generation cars (2016-present) worth £8,000+: a rebuilt engine at £3,000-£5,000 is financially viable and carries a 12-month warranty, which a used engine typically doesn't.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI and 1.5 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.4 TSI (EA111, 2007-2015) is a twincharger (supercharger + turbocharger) with a rear-mounted timing chain and known tensioner weakness. The 1.5 TSI (EA211, 2017-present) is a single-turbo design with a timing belt and updated PCV system. Many UK owners still search 'Tiguan 1.4 TSI' for 1.5 TSI cars, which is why both are covered on this page.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straight engine swap on a Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI typically takes 8-10 hours labour at a specialist, including transfer of ancillary components. 4Motion all-wheel-drive versions add approximately 1 hour due to driveshaft and haldex system disconnection. Most workshops complete the job in 1-2 working days.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: First-generation EA111 1.4 TSI (CAV/CTH) has a known timing chain tensioner weakness that makes it unreliable if not proactively maintained - tensioner failure can occur from 60,000 miles. Second-generation EA211 1.5 TSI (DADA/DPC) is significantly more reliable, with the primary issues being oil consumption on early DADA units and water pump leaks across all EA211 cars.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI arrived with the first-generation Tiguan (Typ 5N) in 2007 as the entry-level petrol option, delivering accessible performance for UK SUV buyers. Over its production life, the 1.4 TSI badge has spanned two engine families - the twincharger EA111 and the turbocharged EA211 - with a 1.5 TSI replacement in second-generation cars from 2017, though UK owners continue to search for "Tiguan 1.4 TSI" across both eras.

milestones.description: First-generation Tiguan (Typ 5N) launches with 1.4 TSI CAV engine, 148hp, supercharged and turbocharged
CAV superseded by CTH 1.4 TSI, 148hp, retaining twincharger design with emissions updates
Facelifted Tiguan continues with CTH 1.4 TSI, now paired with 4Motion AWD on selected trims
End of CTH production for first-generation Tiguan; final year for EA111 1.4 TSI
Second-generation Tiguan (Typ AD/BW) launches - 1.4 TSI badge continues with CWL engine, 148hp, now with turbocharged EA211 architecture replacing the twincharger
1.5 TSI DADA engine introduced, 128hp, replacing CWL
DADA superseded by DPC 1.5 TSI, 148hp, with revised injection and emissions systems
Third-generation Tiguan (Typ AZ) launches with DXG 1.5 eTSI mild-hybrid (148hp); 1.4 TSI badge retired, but used and rebuilt 1.4 TSI demand remains high

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI presents two distinct reliability profiles depending on which engine family you have. First-generation EA111 units (CAV, CTH, 2007-2015) are defined by the notorious timing chain tensioner weakness - a cost-prohibitive repair that frequently tips owners toward replacement. Second-generation EA211 units (CWL, DADA, DPC, DXD, 2016-present) are more robust but bring oil consumption and water pump issues instead. Rebuilt Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components for EA111 units and revised PCV systems for EA211 cars, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI EA111 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The EA111 1.4 TSI uses a rear-mounted timing chain with a plastic tensioner that loses hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack. On cold starts, the chain rattles against guides; ignored long enough, it jumps timing or snaps, destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain kit, tensioner, guides, camshaft sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best before failure - catches it early if you hear cold-start rattle

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has already failed or mileage over 120k - replacement often cheaper than dealer repair

problems.recommendation: If your 1.4 TSI EA111 is already rattling on cold start, book a timing chain inspection immediately. Preventative chain replacement at £800-£1,500 from a specialist is far cheaper than a rebuilt engine. If the chain has already snapped or jumped timing, compare a used engine (under £1,500 fitted if value-conscious) against a rebuilt unit (£2,500-£4,000) - the rebuilt premium buys warranty protection against the same tensioner failure recurring.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CAV CTH Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: High Oil Consumption - Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 1.5 TSI DADA Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4/1.5 TSI (DADA - 2017-2020, early EA211 units)
problems.rootCause: Early EA211 1.5 TSI engines feature a PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) system design that allows excessive oil vapour to be consumed through the intake. Owners report topping up 1 litre of oil every 1,000-2,000 miles; if unaddressed, it leads to carbon buildup and eventual valve damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Revised PCV valve and breather hoses
repairOptions.longevity: First step - often resolves oil consumption on DADA

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake valve decoking - removes baked-on oil deposits
repairOptions.longevity: If PCV replacement doesn't resolve misfires or power loss

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £3,000-£5,000 (matches Section 4's rebuilt price for EA211 proxy)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, updated PCV system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption has caused valve damage or scored bores

problems.vehicleValueCheck: The second-generation Volkswagen Tiguan (Typ AD/BW) with 1.5 TSI typically sits in the £8,000-£22,000 bracket `[THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader UK 2025]`. At this value level, a rebuilt engine is well within the vehicle's worth - the £3,000-£5,000 replacement cost represents 15-40% of vehicle value on most examples, making replacement a viable option over repair.
problems.recommendation: Start with the PCV system replacement (£250-£400 from a specialist) - it resolves the majority of DADA oil consumption cases without needing a full rebuild. If misfires or power loss persist after PCV replacement, carbon cleaning (£300-£600) is the next step. Only consider full replacement if oil consumption exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 miles and borescope inspection confirms cylinder scoring.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DADA Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Leaks - Why the Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4/1.5 TSI EA211 Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4/1.5 TSI (CWL, DADA, DPC - 2016-2024, EA211 units)
problems.rootCause: The EA211 1.4/1.5 TSI water pump housing is made of plastic that degrades with heat cycling, causing slow coolant loss through hairline cracks. If ignored, it leads to overheating and potential head gasket failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New pump, thermostat housing, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Standard repair - most EA211 units will need this once

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £3,000-£5,000 (matches Section 4's rebuilt price for EA211 proxy)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes new water pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if overheating has caused head gasket or bore damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A £400-£800 water pump repair is a routine maintenance cost on any second-generation Tiguan 1.4/1.5 TSI. Even on sub-£8,000 examples, the repair is well within the vehicle's value. Full replacement is not justified for water pump failure alone - only escalate if the engine overheated severely.
problems.recommendation: Do not wait for overheating. If your Volkswagen Tiguan 1.4/1.5 TSI is losing coolant without visible external leaks, suspect the water pump/thermostat housing. Replace it as preventative maintenance around 80,000 miles - £400-£800 from a specialist is a fraction of the cost of a rebuilt engine. If you've already overheated and have persistent misfires or cylinder pressure loss, then compare rebuilt engine prices.
